# Spherical Harmonics Optimization

Also called: SH Optimization, SH Degree Reduction, SH Distillation, SH Vector Quantization

## Overview
Spherical Harmonics (SH) Optimization refers to a family of techniques that modify the storage, representation, or training dynamics of view-dependent color coefficients in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to improve rendering speed, reduce memory footprint, or stabilize optimization. While base 3DGS uses third-order SH (16 coefficients per channel) to model view-dependent appearance, these methods address the associated computational and memory costs. Key approaches include reducing the SH degree via distillation [9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md], compressing coefficients via vector quantization [14181-spherical-harmonics-vector-quantization.md], or optimizing the training process itself to handle multi-view gradients more efficiently [13982-efficient-multi-view-training-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation, where the scene is defined by a set of $N$ 3D Gaussians $\{G_i\}_{i=1}^N$. Each Gaussian $G_i$ is defined by its mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$, covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (derived from rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{S}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and view-dependent color $\mathbf{c}_i(\omega)$.

The rendering process evaluates the Gaussian density along a ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\omega$ and integrates contributions. The Gaussian density function is:
$$ G(\mathbf{x}) = \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu})^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1} (\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu})\right) $$

The core variation across methods lies in the definition, storage, and optimization of $\mathbf{c}_i(\omega)$ and potentially $\alpha_i$, moving beyond the fixed SH coefficients used in base 3DGS. Common strategies include:
1.  **Post-Processing Transformation:** Applying a learned affine transformation to the rendered image based on 3D position and view embedding [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].
2.  **Factorized Illumination:** Separating scene lighting (via a tensor grid) from material properties (via BRDF features) to model specular effects [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].
3.  **Image-Conditioned Modulation:** Using an MLP and per-image embeddings to modulate Gaussian color and opacity, enabling transient object removal and appearance synthesis [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].
4.  **Neural Field Substitution:** Replacing per-Gaussian SH with a shared grid-based neural field to reduce parameters and improve generalization [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].
5.  **Volumetric Attenuation:** Modifying the alpha-blending equation to incorporate medium properties, such as direct attenuation $B_d$ and backscatter parameters $B_\infty, B_b$, to model light transport in non-vacuum media [15148-physics-and-optical-modeling.md].

## Subtopics

### [First-order Spherical Harmonics Distillation](9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md)
Reduces the SH degree from third-order to first-order to decrease parameter count and computation cost, enabling real-time rendering on mobile devices [9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md]. It differs from standard SH degree reduction by employing a distillation strategy where a student model with first-order SH approximates the directional radiance of a pretrained third-order teacher model, rather than simply truncating coefficients [9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md]. This approach minimizes the quality loss associated with aggressive compression, achieving a 61% reduction in parameters and 52% reduction in computation with only a 0.48 dB PSNR drop [9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md].

### [Explicit Camera Jacobian Derivation](10077-explicit-camera-jacobian-derivation.md)
Derives analytical Jacobians of the SE(3) camera pose with respect to 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) primitives to enable efficient gradient-based camera tracking [10077-explicit-camera-jacobian-derivation.md]. It solves the problem of high computational overhead and redundant parameterization inherent in automatic differentiation when optimizing camera poses in SLAM systems. Unlike prior ray-intersection methods that assume fewer Gaussians, this approach provides the first analytical Jacobians for EWA splatting and 3DGS, ensuring the Jacobian dimensionality matches the six degrees of freedom of the Lie algebra [10077-explicit-camera-jacobian-derivation.md].

### [Efficient Multi-View Training for 3D Gaussian Splatting](13982-efficient-multi-view-training-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md)
Enables stable optimization of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by training on multiple images per iteration, addressing the high variance of gradients inherent in the standard single-view approach [13982-efficient-multi-view-training-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md]. While standard 3DGS renders one image per iteration due to rasterization overhead, this method uses thread-efficient partial rendering to gather pixels from multiple views without idle thread waste, reducing mini-batch gradient variance and improving convergence stability compared to [Spherical Harmonics Optimization](14206-spherical-harmonics-optimization.md) and [First-order Spherical Harmonics Distillation](9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md) [13982-efficient-multi-view-training-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

### [Spherical Harmonics Vector Quantization](14181-spherical-harmonics-vector-quantization.md)
SH VQ is a compression technique for 3D Gaussian Splatting that replaces per-splat SH coefficients with indices pointing to a shared palette of distinct SH vectors, reducing memory footprint at the cost of minor lighting artifacts [14181-spherical-harmonics-vector-quantization.md]. It differs from [First-order Spherical Harmonics Distillation](9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md) by retaining full SH basis functions (rather than reducing to first-order) and from [Explicit Camera Jacobian Derivation](10077-explicit-camera-jacobian-derivation.md) by focusing on storage compression rather than gradient computation. It is chosen when memory bandwidth or storage size is the primary bottleneck and view-dependent specular effects must be preserved better than simple color quantization allows [14181-spherical-harmonics-vector-quantization.md].

### [Closed-Form Scene Appearance Estimation](16750-closed-form-scene-appearance-estimation.md)
Estimates spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients for mesh vertices by solving a global weighted least-squares problem that jointly fits RGB observations from all calibrated views [16750-closed-form-scene-appearance-estimation.md]. It distinguishes itself from iterative optimization approaches by providing an analytical closed-form solution, utilizing adaptive regularization to constrain SH bands based on the directional support available at each vertex [16750-closed-form-scene-appearance-estimation.md].

### [Adaptive SH Regularization](16786-adaptive-sh-regularization.md)
A regularization strategy that suppresses non-DC (higher-order, l > 0) SH components for vertices with insufficient directional support, while preserving the DC (l = 0) component, to prevent overfitting under sparse or uneven observations [16750-closed-form-scene-appearance-estimation.md].

### SH Degree Zero Optimization
- **Definition:** Setting the maximum degree of Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients to 0 to remove superfluous operations and improve training speed, as higher-degree SH coefficients for color remain unchanged during training [S1, unofficial].
- **Step:** Modify the model code to delete operations relative to the max degree in the model and set the max degree parameter to 0 [S1, unofficial].
- **Pitfall:** In the original 3D Gaussian Splatting model, features represented by SH coefficients with degree > 0 are unchanged during all training, making them useless [S1, unofficial].
- **Number:** Directly changing the max degree to 0 yields a 16.25% improvement compared to the default. With specific changing code, it yields a 16.57% improvement but increases CPU-GPU process time [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation uses third-order SH to model view-dependent appearance [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md]. However, this results in significant memory and computational overhead. Subsequent research has focused on optimizing this representation. SH Degree Zero Optimization was proposed to address the observation that higher-degree SH coefficients often remain static during training, suggesting they may be redundant for certain scenes [S1, unofficial]. Distillation methods leverage pretrained high-fidelity models to train compact low-degree representations [9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md]. Vector quantization techniques adapt codebook-based compression to the high-dimensional SH space [14181-spherical-harmonics-vector-quantization.md]. Analytical Jacobian derivations address the inefficiencies of automatic differentiation in camera pose optimization [10077-explicit-camera-jacobian-derivation.md]. Multi-view training strategies aim to stabilize the optimization landscape by reducing gradient variance [13982-efficient-multi-view-training-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md]. Closed-form estimation provides an alternative to iterative optimization for mesh-based appearance modeling [16750-closed-form-scene-appearance-estimation.md].
